title: Box-Bound Ruler
subtitle: Even a paintbox can brew a storm.

trails.title: "Pride and Prejudice"
trails.description: If you harbor any prejudice toward artists, by all means, hold on to it.

content.text:
Calvaire - 1920.10.06

Ledru-Rollin - 1920.10.10

Richard Lenoir - 1920.10.13

Fitzwilliam - 1920.10.19

Taira - 1920.10.21

Larisa - 1920.10.21

Diggers - 1920.10.23

items.text: Performers and audience members leave one by one. The wild night falls back into silence.
Under the dark sky, a person carrying secrets takes a careful, winding path before knocking on the side of a courtyard gate.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: I've come as requested, Ms. Butterfly.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: I ensured I wasn't followed by any—

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: I have cameras set up. I would've known if you were. Shut up and get in.
Abandoned Room

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: We've been waiting here for an hour.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: "We"?

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: We have company. Your employer, in fact. Allow me to introduce you to "Mr. Pérez."

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: The mysterious mastermind behind the Turquoise Serpent Club.
She smiles and opens the battered pigment case in front of her.
The mice, waiting for this moment, lunge out in a desperate attack against their kidnapper.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: This is our chance, my children! Kill the bipedal monster!
The pointless fight ends. Bruised and battered, the little mice are tossed back into the case.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: Argh! Kitty claws! Just who the hell are you, biped?!

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: Did Cruz send you? Oh, I get it now. You're with Miguel, aren't you?

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: He's bent out of shape about the auction. Thinks I'm stepping on his block. Tch!

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: How much did he pay you, huh? I'll offer double, no, triple! Or are you with the government? If so, I'm open to negotiating a very handsome price for your cooperation.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Huh, it's hard not to find the sight of a rodent begging for its life amusing.
The smile she flashes down at them borders on unhinged. In response, the pleading mouse turns to the other face.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: Wait a second. You—I know you, boy! You're Añil, the one I hired to forge paintings for the club!

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: How dare you betray me, you furless cretin!

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: Miss, you really mean to claim that they are Pérez?

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: The legendary Pérez, the feared boss who controls the Turquoise Serpent Club and most of Mexico City's black market with an iron fist?
A wave of absurdity washes over him, though he can't bring himself to laugh.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: An iron fist, gripped in the paws of a few tiny mice.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: If I'm correct, these little troublemakers managed to replace the real Pérez about a month ago.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Since then, they've stayed hidden, mimicking Pérez's voice from behind a screen. No one's noticed until now.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: No wonder the club's started making so many strange moves.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Yes. Under their leadership, the club has absorbed several gangs and expanded its influence in the black market. It was their idea to start forging all those paintings and hold the auction.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Hm. If you ask me, they've far outdone the original Pérez.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Oh, the irony. Any tears coming?
He refuses to answer.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: Oye, you're right. The club's recent success is all thanks to me.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: See what we mice can do? How great we are! No one knows how to run a gang better than a rodent.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: You know why? Because you giant two-leggers don't have a head for this business, while we brilliant burrowers were born to rule the underground.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: I don't recall asking for your opinion.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Come to think of it, I need only one mouse for my purposes, one that's quiet and obedient.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: As for the rest, I happen to have a colleague who enjoys nothing more than feasting on rats. Eight of them, actually. We're not close, but I'm sure you'd make a perfect gift.
She hovers her hand over the case, letting her fingers dangle above them menacingly and fall like a claw machine in search of a toy.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: W-W-Wait! Leave my children out of this, please!

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: I-I apologize for my rudeness, miss. Clearly, you're an extraordinary arcanist, unlike most of your cheese-brained kind.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: You deserve to rule the underworld just as much as I do. I'll gladly hand you this club on a silver platter if that's what you desire.
It is exactly what she wants to hear. In a split second, her face turns from menace to quiet satisfaction.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Hm. Rodents are quite adaptable when they need to be.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: But I'm not interested in running a gang.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: Surely there's something I can help you with, miss. You're looking for a pigment, aren't you?

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: I'll tell you everything I know, all of it, just as long as you guarantee my children's safety.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: Though the odds of finding that particular arcane pigment again are a million to one. In any case, let's start from the beginning.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: We mice are, of course, far superior to all humankind. I don't refute it. But not every mouse has got the smarts that my family does. What made my children and me so special, you ask? It all began with a squeak-tacular accident.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: On a frightening, fateful night, as I ran for my life from a snarling hellbeast, the true nemesis of mousekind, I found myself in an unfamiliar room.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: The floor was so clean I nearly slipped, and the furniture gave off a rich, soothing scent. But the walls above, good heavens, they were covered with the heads of beasts beyond any counting!

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: Still, I pulled myself together and climbed up onto the dining table, hoping to find something to eat. Who would have thought there'd be nothing but a small plate of glowing pigment up there?

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: The pigment looked odd, I admit, but my hunger overtook my fear, so I ate it. And the moment it touched my tongue, the world as I knew it fell away.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: For the first time in my life, I had other thoughts beyond mating and eating, beyond survival! Thoughts that only true intelligence could evoke!

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: I stayed there for a couple more days, and thanks to my keen eye, I learned I was in this Pérez's office, and that he ran half of Mexico City's smuggling business.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: A strange masked person in a black robe brought him that miraculous substance. It seems, at their request, Pérez was using a lumber mill as a front while they extracted a unique silver ore from Valle de Lágrimas—the Vale of Tears.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: The masked person refined the ore into a pigment and had it shipped far away, to lands they called "Yu-Rope" and "Yu-Ess." And in return, the club received a portion of it.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: To get my hands on the pigment, and Pérez's smuggling business on the side, I staged a coup. We replaced him without even breaking a sweat.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: Further proof that you bipeds are far duller than us brilliant, quadrupedal mice!

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: Everything was going smoothly, and we had a steady supply of pigment, until that masked stranger up and vanished, taking the secret to its creation with them!

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: I turned the city upside down, trying to track them down. I thought no one could hide themselves from me.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: But they did—poof! Gone without a trace. Like they never even existed.
The little mouse finishes with an excited flourish. Her listeners pause, each deep in contemplation. Añil speaks first.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: It must be because of the Vale of Tears' silver ore. I've heard of it before.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: The locals called the place the Man-Eating Maw. Every miner who ventured into its tunnels never returned.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: In the 18th century, there was a massive mine collapse. No one's managed to find any silver there since.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: Rumor is the silver they found there shimmers with an extraordinary glow and is highly malleable, two qualities that make it an exceptionally rare alchemical material.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: But I've never heard of it being made into a pigment, let alone it being used to grant mice intelligence.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: As I'm sure you've noticed, miss, my children, they no longer speak as I do.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: It seems the intelligence granted by the pigment must be maintained through regular consumption.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: Without it, they've turned back into ordinary mice, one after the other.
The young mice stare up at their mother with blank faces, frightened but unaware.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: The same tragedy will befall me soon. I can feel it. Whether in a month or a matter of weeks.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: No, I won't let that happen.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: That explains your recent desperation.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Rushing the auction, expanding your smuggling operation, all in search of a substitute for this arcane pigment.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: But your efforts were in vain. How sad, hmph.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: Oye, miss, you think rubbing salt in a victim's wound is fun?

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: It is one of my hobbies.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: So, Manus Vindictae must've last appeared about a month ago.
She puts it together quickly. All of this must have happened shortly after the "Storm" reset the era to the 1920s.

Manus Vindictae arrived, already aware of the hidden mine that had yet to be discovered during this period, with the alchemical knowledge necessary to refine its bounty into the very mineral pigment that she had been searching for.
The Institutum researcher weighs her next move.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: I will help you. But you need to tell me the exact identities of every Manus member who's dealt with the club.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: Well, it's not that I don't want to tell you, but even I, the ever-resourceful Pérez, know little about them. I doubt you'll be able to smoke them out either.
Still doubtful but very much cowed with fear, she takes out a list and hands it over.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Calvaire, Richard Lenoir, Ledru-Rollin, Fitzwilliam, Taira, Diggers ...

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Just aliases, not their real names.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: Deliberately cryptic aliases at that! Freakish bipeds.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: They came to this city discreetly, disguised as tourists, journalists, or some harmless arcane society members.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: They never stayed long. Once a batch of pigment was ready, they vanished soon after. I even asked a friend in the government to help track them down, but they couldn't find any trace of them.
Lorentz Butterfly scans through the names, searching for a glimmer of recognition.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Fitzwilliam.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Where else have I seen that name? Besides Pride and Prejudice?

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: Fitzwilliam? That fellow claimed to be a "cultural journalist" who came to the city to write reports about local festivals.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: He isn't just good with a pen, though. He's a skilled smuggler. So skilled, in fact, that his slippery fingers also made off with quite a few valuables from my club.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Ah yes, that report.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: It seems likely that to get the foreign diplomat to agree to the interview, he offered him something from the club as a gift.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Our "Mr. Darcy" has already left the city, but the diplomat will stay until the end of the festival.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: The key to everything lies in that gift.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: The gift? Why bother with that? Isn't the pigment what we're really after?

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: Or do you mean the diplomat is a Manus member too? Is the gift itself the pigment?

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Once we find the answer to one, we'll uncover the answer to the other.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: I-If you're sure we're on the right track, I'll do all I can to help you out.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: Our grand operation to retake the pigment will start at sunrise tomorrow. No, make that now. What are you waiting for? Free me so I can gather my men and—

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: You're not going anywhere, Mr. Pérez.
The correction comes with a cold smile.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: You won't be part of this operation. And don't even dream about freedom until I get my hands on the pigment.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Better pray I solve this before you lose the last of your wits like your kids.

items.speaker: Mamá Pérez
items.text: No! You can't do this to me, you two-legged demon!
She lowers the lid of the pigment case down, slow yet firm, until their cries become muffled squeaks once more. Then she flips the latch down.
She walks to the window to take in the last moments of the night.

A dry night wind blows through the city as the day dawns on the Day of the Dead. The mask of menace she had worn through her interrogation is gone entirely. All that's left is a woman staring out a window, content but unsmiling.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: You seem confident, Ms. Butterfly.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: You've already found some critical clues pointing to things beyond this pigment, haven't you?

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Yes, something that connects all the murders.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: And a soon-to-be victim. Alive, for the time being.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: Incredible! You pieced it all together from just a single glance at that list?

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: But shouldn't you do something right away? You might still be able to save them.
In response, she passes him the list dryly over her shoulder.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: "Save them"? Why would I do that?

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Don't bother trying to figure me out. Wastes both our time. The murders, the Vigiles, the gangs, and this whole underground world mean nothing to me.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: This drama will draw its curtain tomorrow, All Souls' Day, when the city's residents welcome back their departed faithful.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: Interrupting such a heartfelt occasion would just be cruel, don't you think?

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: No, I'll infiltrate the diplomat's mansion tomorrow night and attend the festival myself, though I guarantee you won't be able to find me in the crowd.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: When the killer strikes and the audience screams, I'll be sitting in the best seat in the house.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: And prove, as always, that my deductions are flawless.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: I think I see your reasoning now, Ms. Butterfly.
The large device she carries makes an audible hum, only noticeable in the silence between them.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: Pardon me for asking, but what is this device you're carrying about?

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: A "Demonic Scale"-based additive manufacturing machine, powered by tens of thousands of arcane skills operating simultaneously.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: I've never seen such technology.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: In layman's terms, you might think of it as a kind of automatic arcane printer for physical items.

items.speaker: Lorentz Butterfly
items.text: But it's merely a prop for tomorrow night's performance.
An ornate letter engraved on its casing catches his eye.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: M, the initial of your name, isn't it, miss?

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: What does it stand for? Mystery? Madness? Magic?
Each guess slides off of her unanswered.

items.speaker: Añil
items.text: Mary? Mia? Mona, perhaps?
M—
Marguerite.
